set_aside.subject: backup snapshot instant
set_aside.text: A18 says “its recorded instant … [is] when its read transaction began” and State 3 says the copy answers “the instant that transaction began”; the change instead says “the instant is read from the clock at [the first audit-counter] read,” and the flow repeats that the instant is read “at” the read that fixes the snapshot.
set_aside.question: Is the backup's recorded instant the beginning of the read transaction or the later first read of the audit counter that fixes its snapshot?
options: Record the instant when the read transaction begins.
Record the instant when the first audit-counter read fixes the snapshot.
set_aside.default_guess: Use the instant of the first audit-counter read, because that is the newly added rule and ties the metadata to the actual snapshot boundary.

witness.initial: A daily backup run has opened its SQLite read transaction, but it has not yet made the audit-counter read; the wall clock advances between those events.
events: module:store begins the backup's read transaction at 03:00:00.
Another action commits while the read transaction has made no read.
module:store first reads the audit counter at 03:00:01, fixing the SQLite snapshot.
outcomes: An implementation following “when its read transaction began” records 03:00:00.
An implementation following “the instant is read from the clock at that read” records 03:00:01.
witness.observer: The owner sees the differing newest-backup instant; backup naming, age calculation, and the interpretation of which committed changes precede its recorded instant also differ.
